image_description: A close-up, slightly high-angle shot of a realistic Triceratops model or statue standing on a dark surface. The subject is a quadrupedal dinosaur with textured, brownish-grey skin, large hexagonal scales, and yellowish accents on the frill and beak. It features three prominent horns and a large bony frill. A black support stand is visible beneath the belly, and a small white card lies on the floor near the front right foot.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Three prominent horns: two long brow horns projecting forward and upward above the eyes, and a shorter nasal horn on the snout.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image clearly displays two large brow horns curving forward/upward and a smaller, distinct nasal horn on the snout. The morphology matches the diagnostic description perfectly.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Beak is parrot-like with a sharp, keratinous cutting edge.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The anterior part of the skull forms a distinct, curved beak structure typical of ceratopsians, appearing sharp and well-defined.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is quadrupedal with columnar, elephant-like limbs.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The subject stands on four thick, pillar-like legs that resemble elephant limbs in girth and posture, supporting the heavy body mass.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Enormous bony frill (neck shield) extending posteriorly from the skull, with width dramatically exceeding the skull itself.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The frill is massive, extending widely behind the head and clearly wider than the facial portion of the skull. It dominates the upper rear profile.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Frill is solid bone with a smooth outer surface and possible epoccipital (marginal) bumps.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The frill appears solid (no large holes/fenestrations visible in this angle) and features distinct rounded bumps (epoccipitals) along the marginal edge, consistent with the description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is inferred to have been covered in large, hexagonal scales with possible quill-like structures along the back and tail.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The texture of the model shows detailed, large polygonal/hexagonal scaling patterns across the body and legs. No obvious quills are visible, but the scale pattern is prominent and accurate to modern interpretations.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Forelimbs are shorter than hindlimbs creating a sloping backline.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The shoulder height is visibly lower than the hip height, creating the characteristic downward slope from rear to front typical of Triceratops anatomy.

The tail is largely occluded by the angle of the photo and the framing cuts off the posterior end of the animal. Only the very base might be inferred, but it cannot be rigorously tested for length or stoutness.

artifact_observations.location: Under the belly/center of the subject
artifact_observations.reasoning: A thin black vertical rod (support stand) is visible holding up the model. This is an artifact of the object being a physical statue/model rather than a living creature, but not an AI generation error. It indicates the image is likely a photograph of a prop.
A small white rectangular card or tag is lying on the floor. This is a real-world object inconsistent with a natural habitat scene, further confirming this is a photo of a model/display.
